questions.title: Rectangle Area with a Class
questions.description:
OOP starts by bundling data and behavior together. Define a class Rectangle with two fields length and width and a method area() that returns length * width. In main, read the two values, store them in a Rectangle object, and print the area returned by the object's method.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated numbers: length and width.

Output Format:
Print one line: the rectangle area rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
0 < length, width <= 10000

questions.title: Student Profile Display
questions.description:
Define a class Student with three fields: name (String), rollNo (int) and marks (int). Give the class a method display() that prints the three fields, one per line. In main, read the values, fill a Student object, and call display().

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated values: name rollNo marks (name is one word).

Output Format:
Line 1: Name: <name>
Line 2: Roll: <rollNo>
Line 3: Marks: <marks>

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 50, 1 <= rollNo <= 9999, 0 <= marks <= 100

questions.title: Private Counter Taps
questions.description:
Encapsulation keeps a field safe inside a class. Define a class Counter with a private int field count starting at 0, a method increment() that adds 1 to count, and a method getCount() that returns count. In main, read n, create one Counter object, call increment() exactly n times, and print the final value through getCount().

Input Format:
A single line with one integer n.

Output Format:
Print one line: the counter value after n increments.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000

questions.title: Book Summary Line
questions.description:
Define a class Book with private fields title, author and price. Provide a method setDetails(String t, String a, double p) to fill them and a method summary() that returns the line: title by author costs P.PP (price with 2 decimals). In main, read title, author and price, fill the book through setDetails, and print book.summary().

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated values: title author price (title and author are single words).

Output Format:
Print one line exactly as returned by summary(): <title> by <author> costs <price with 2 decimals>.

Constraints:
1 <= title, author length <= 50, 0 <= price <= 100000

questions.title: Circle Circumference Class
questions.description:
Define a class Circle with a field radius and a method circumference() that returns 2 * Math.PI * radius. In main, read the radius, store it in a Circle object, and print the circumference returned by the object's method.

Input Format:
A single line with one number, the radius r.

Output Format:
Print one line: the circumference rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
0 < r <= 10000

questions.title: Dog Extends Animal Demo
questions.description:
Inheritance lets one class reuse another's members. Define a class Animal with a field name and a method eat() that prints: <name> eats food. Define a class Dog that extends Animal and adds a method bark() that prints: <name> barks. In main, read the dog's name, store it in a Dog object, then call eat() (inherited from Animal) and bark() (defined in Dog itself).

Input Format:
A single line with one word: the dog's name.

Output Format:
Line 1: <name> eats food
Line 2: <name> barks

Constraints:
1 <= name length <= 50

questions.title: Bank Deposit Only Account
questions.description:
A new bank account starts empty. Define a class BankAccount with a private double field balance starting at 0.0, a method deposit(double amount) that adds to the balance, and a method getBalance() that returns it. In main, read n and then n deposit amounts, perform the deposits in order on one account object, and print the final balance.

Input Format:
A single line: n followed by n space-separated deposit amounts.

Output Format:
Print one line: the final balance rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 100, 0 <= deposit amount <= 100000

questions.title: Employee Profile Card
questions.description:
An office portal prints a small profile card for every employee. Define a class Employee with fields name (String), department (String) and salary (double), plus a method printCard() that prints three lines: Employee: <name>, then Department: <department>, then Salary: <salary with 2 decimals>. In main, read the values, fill the object, and call printCard().

Input Format:
A single line with three space-separated values: name department salary.

Output Format:
Line 1: Employee: <name>
Line 2: Department: <department>
Line 3: Salary: <salary with 2 decimals>

Constraints:
1 <= name, department length <= 50, 0 <= salary <= 1000000

questions.title: Point Distance from Origin
questions.description:
A well-designed class hides how a result is computed. Define a class Point with fields x and y and a method distanceFromOrigin() that returns Math.sqrt(x * x + y * y). In main, read the coordinates, store them in a Point object, and print whatever the object's method returns. main only asks the object for the distance; the formula stays hidden inside the class.

Input Format:
A single line with two space-separated numbers: x and y.

Output Format:
Print one line: the distance from the origin rounded to exactly 2 decimal places.

Constraints:
-1000 <= x, y <= 1000

questions.title: Pet Voices via Base Reference
questions.description:
Two different pet objects answer the same call differently. Define a base class Pet with a field name and a method speak() that returns some default sound. Define class Dog extends Pet with speak() returning Woof, and class Cat extends Pet with speak() returning Meow. Read two pets (type then name each), keep both objects in Pet variables, and for each print: <name> says <what speak() returns>.

Input Format:
A single line with four space-separated tokens: type1 name1 type2 name2, where each type is Dog or Cat.

Output Format:
Line 1: <name1> says <sound1>
Line 2: <name2> says <sound2>

Constraints:
Each type is Dog or Cat; 1 <= name length <= 50
